strings.name: Norman Foster
strings.role: Architect · Structure, technology and urban public space
strings.summary: Foster studied architecture in Manchester and at Yale before founding his practice. He helped develop high-tech architecture by combining engineering structure, flexible space and energy-conscious design. Hong Kong’s HSBC building, the Reichstag transformation and London’s Gherkin work at different scales; Apple Park extends the approach to a large workplace campus. The 1999 Pritzker laureate continues discussing transport, public space and urban life.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1935–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Influenced architectural practice worldwide through high-tech architecture and major urban projects, addressing structural expression, energy use and the organization of public space.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Architecture degree, University of Manchester; Master of Architecture, Yale University
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Engineering as architectural expression
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Projects such as HSBC in Hong Kong make structure and services part of a building’s identity while exploring adaptable large spaces.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Historic buildings and public space
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The Reichstag transformation used a glass dome and visitor routes to reorganize a historic building alongside its environmental performance and use.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses London and the future of cities
strings.timeline.event-01.text: A new NLA interview addressed public space, transport, collaboration and younger talent; the award ceremony remained scheduled for November.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Apple Park begins occupation
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The campus designed with Apple began phased occupation, organizing its workplace around a ring-shaped building, landscape and energy systems.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: 30 St Mary Axe is completed
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Its curved profile, diagonal structure and environmental strategies reshaped the office tower and became a City of London landmark.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Reichstag transformation and Pritzker recognition
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Berlin’s Reichstag reopened with a new dome and parliamentary spaces; Foster received the Pritzker Prize that year.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: HSBC’s Hong Kong headquarters opens
strings.timeline.event-05.text: An exposed suspended structure and flexible interior defined a new bank-building model; the main construction phase had finished in 1985.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Sainsbury Centre is completed
strings.timeline.event-06.text: A long-span structure at the University of East Anglia combined art collections, teaching and public activity in a flexible cultural building.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Establishes Foster Associates
strings.timeline.event-07.text: He founded his own practice in Britain, developing earlier collaborative experience into an international architectural team.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes graduate studies at Yale
strings.timeline.event-08.text: A scholarship enabled him to gain a master’s degree after his Manchester education, broadening his architectural and engineering perspective.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Greater Manchester
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Stockport and raised in Manchester, he developed an interest in technology and architecture amid early work and an industrial city.
